correctness.rationale: Each maximal consecutive run gives a full interval of base-g block values for one summand and an interval through exactly one additional carry position for g summands. Inter-run extended blocks are disjoint. The finite-prefix periodic densities multiply exactly. If their limit is zero, upper density is zero; if positive, finitely many long gaps and summable missing-block residue fractions imply via a uniform 3x tail bound that ordinary natural density equals the product. Exactly g positive summands differ from zero-permitted summands only when the total of all block coordinates is less than g, a set of size \(O_g((1+\log x)^{g-1})\) below x. For \(h<g\), the standard carry bound h-1 forces each excluded digit to lie in a strict subset of possible digits, implying density zero. Exact finite verification succeeds in seven distinct digit masks over bases 2,3,4. The infinite proof is not inferred from experiments.

value.rationale: The 2026 source identifies the equal-base/summand boundary as structurally important. The result classifies the natural density, including its existence and a complete iff positive-density criterion, for a natural infinite family with arbitrary allowed digit-position runs. It demonstrates a sharp transition between density zero for every \(h<g\) and potentially near-full density at \(h=g\), despite infinitely many missing allowed exponents. The proof also distinguishes ordinary density from periodic-cylinder or finite counting heuristics; this is a meaningful structural characterization rather than a routine finite table.
